title: Similar Triangles: AA, SSS, SAS and Proportions
seo_title: Similar Triangles Worksheet: AA, SSS, SAS, Side Splitter (Geometry, G-SRT.B.5) | 100 Questions
standard_text: Use congruence and similarity criteria for triangles to solve problems and to prove relationships in geometric figures.
meta_desc: Free Geometry worksheet on similar triangles: AA, SSS and SAS similarity, nested triangles, the Triangle Proportionality Theorem, geometric mean and shadows. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: AA, SSS~ and SAS~ prove triangles similar.
key_sub: If DE ∥ BC, then AD/DB = AE/EC. Use the whole side when comparing the small and large triangles.
body_html:
How it works

Triangles are similar when their angles are congruent and their sides are proportional. Three shortcuts prove it:

  • AA: two pairs of congruent angles.
  • SSS~: all three pairs of sides in the same ratio.
  • SAS~: two pairs of sides in the same ratio and the angles between them congruent.

If DE ∥ BC, then △ADE ~ △ABC, and AD/DB = AE/EC (Triangle Proportionality Theorem). When you compare the small and large triangles, use the whole side AB = AD + DB.

In a right triangle, the altitude to the hypotenuse makes two smaller similar triangles: CD² = AD × DB, and AC² = AD × AB.

Example

DE ∥ BC, AD = 4, DB = 6 and DE = 5. Find BC.

AB = 4 + 6 = 10

BC/5 = 10/4

Answer: BC = 12.5

Example

A 6 ft person casts a 4 ft shadow, and a tree casts a 30 ft shadow. How tall is the tree?

6/4 = h/30

Answer: 45 ft

Common mistakes

  • Using DB instead of the whole side AB when comparing △ADE with △ABC.
  • Calling triangles similar by SSA or by one pair of angles.
  • Matching sides in the wrong order. Match shortest to shortest and longest to longest.
  • Using the whole hypotenuse in CD² = AD × DB. Use the two segments.

faq.q: How do you prove triangles are similar?
faq.a: Use AA (two pairs of congruent angles), SSS similarity (all sides proportional) or SAS similarity (two sides proportional with the included angle congruent).

faq.q: What is the Triangle Proportionality Theorem?
faq.a: If a line parallel to one side of a triangle crosses the other two sides, it divides them proportionally.

faq.q: What is the geometric mean in a right triangle?
faq.a: The altitude to the hypotenuse is the geometric mean of the two hypotenuse segments: h² = (segment 1)(segment 2).

faq.q: How do shadows show similar triangles?
faq.a: At the same time of day, the sun's rays hit objects at the same angle, so each object and its shadow form similar right triangles.

items.q: △ABC has angles of 59° and 40°. △DEF has angles of 40° and 81°. Are the triangles similar?
items.e: The third angle of △ABC is 81°, so both triangles have angles 59°, 40° and 81°. Two pairs of congruent angles: Yes, by AA similarity.

items.q: △ABC has angles of 47° and 61°. △DEF has angles of 61° and 72°. Are the triangles similar?
items.e: The third angle of △ABC is 72°, so both triangles have angles 47°, 61° and 72°. Two pairs of congruent angles: Yes, by AA similarity.

items.q: △ABC has sides 9, 12 and 14. △DEF has sides 18, 24 and 29. Are the triangles similar?
items.e: 18 ÷ 9 = 2, but 29 ÷ 14 = 29/14. The ratios are not all equal. No.

items.q: △ABC has sides 3, 10 and 12. △DEF has sides 6, 20 and 24. Are the triangles similar?
items.e: Shortest to shortest, middle to middle, longest to longest: every ratio is 2. Yes, by SSS similarity.

items.e: The angles match, but 24 ÷ 8 ≠ 29 ÷ 9, so the sides are not proportional. No.

items.q: Noah is 6 ft tall and casts a 3 ft shadow. At the same time, a building casts a 48 ft shadow. How tall is the building?
items.e: The sun's rays make similar triangles: height/shadow is the same. 6/3 = h/48, so h = 6 × 48 ÷ 3 = 96 ft.

items.q: A 4 ft post casts a 3 ft shadow. A nearby tower casts a 30 ft shadow. How tall is the tower?
items.e: Heights and shadows are proportional: 4/3 = h/30, so h = 40 ft.

items.q: Ava puts a mirror on the ground 4 ft from herself and 18 ft from a wall. Her eyes are 6 ft above the ground, and she sees the top of a sign on the wall in the mirror. How high is the top of the sign?
items.e: The angles at the mirror are equal, so the triangles are similar: 6/4 = h/18, h = 27 ft.
